original.description: The overall goal of ARTES 4.0 Business Applications can be summarised as the development of pre-operational services - possibly in partnership - for a wide range of users through the combination of different systems. Business Applications activities aim at: i) collecting user feedback for better tuning of the applications and the operation of all elements involved, ii) developing commercial sustainable space based applications by linking user needs to corresponding solutions incorporating space assets requesting only limited technology adaptations, iii) demonstrating to users and stakeholders that the proposed solutions work in their operational environment and are compatible with their operational practices, iv) utilising at least one space asset (such as Satellite Communications, Earth Observation, Satellite Navigation, Human Spaceflight, or any other space asset, service or technology), leading to a better exploitation of existing space capacity and know-how together with a better understanding of how they should evolve to respond to user needs. ARTES 4.0 Business Applications operates via a 'Call for Proposals' which is always open. Partners respond with proposals as they find it opportune. The activities proposed in response to this 'Call for Proposals' must be relevant to above mentioned ARTES 4.0 Business Applications objectives. Although not a competitive tender action, this Call for Proposals' is published on esa-star Publication in order to achieve a higher degree of visibility. The closing date that is mentioned upon issue of the Call for Proposals is established solely for technical reasons connected with the esa-star Publication system and can be disregarded.

original.description: The ACCESS (Accelerating Commercialisation and Competitiveness of the European Space Sector) programme helps companies develop innovative commercial products and services that strengthen European competitiveness in both space and non-space markets. It fosters a diverse and dynamic space ecosystem, ensuring that the benefits of commercialisation reach all Participating States.Business Applications and Space Solutions (BASS) is the element of ACCESS programme specifically designed to accelerate the transformation of innovative ideas into market-ready space-based services and applications that deliver measurable socio-economic impact.BASS offers to companies and academia derisking tools to mitigate technical and commercial risks, shortening the path from concept to market. With a strong user-driven focus, BASS creates the conditions for commercial success and positions space as a driver of innovation, competitiveness, and lasting value for society.To deliver these outcomes, BASS offers a comprehensive support package which includes zero-equity funding, tailored business and technical expertise, project management guidance, ESA branding, and access to commercialisation networks. This ecosystem connects companies with customers, investors, and partners, enabling them to overcome market barriers whilesecuring sustainable growth through private investment and demand-driven adoption.BASS support is tailored to every stage of developmentfrom assessing the viability of new space-based applications, to designing, implementing, and piloting space-based solutions and supporting their expansion into new markets.

original.description: Under NAVISP Element 2, the Agency issues this permanently open Standard Call for Proposals without procurement, using Cooperative Agreements as contractual instrument.This Standard Call for Proposals without procurement aims to enhance Participant States' industrial competitiveness in the evolving Positioning, Navigation, and Timing (PNT) sector. Industry is invited to submit proposals to develop innovative and competitive PNT-related products. The Agency accepts proposals from both space and non-space companies, including large companies, mid-caps, small enterprises, and start-ups. Proposed products may address the satellite space segment, ground infrastructure, and user segment, including applications and services. Industry and research institutes of Participant States are encouraged to contact the NAVISP Element 2 team to discuss the development of pre-operational products aligned with their strategiesand plans. Details on the tendering process and how to prepare the Full Proposal are provided in the Standard Call for Proposals without procurement documentation.

original.description: The European Space Agency ("the Agency" or "ESA") invites you to submit a Proposal under the General Support Technology Programme, Element 1: "Preparation of enabling space technologies and building blocks''The aim is to prepare and to develop enabling capabilities and the associated building blocks for space related systems and the associated sub-systems. An additional aim is to allow the targeted and coordinated development of the capabilities and building blocks (i.e. among academia and industry) in a given ESA Member State or across different Member States (in a collaborative manner). The intended output is to provide industry with a stronger foundation (i.e. building on this acquired know-how) in order to contribute to new space related system opportunities at national or international levels (institutional, commercial...) The objective is to enable Member States to support the further development of t capabilities and the associated building blocks in their industry. The technology development activities may be prepared in a targeted and coordinated manner. The enabling capabilities and building blocks are to be developed for a targeted type and class of space systems (in terms of performance, cost, size...) and with guiding specifications. The developments are to be performed in a coordinated manner to ensure that industry is able to work on complementary capabilities. The developments may be performed within one Member State or across several Member States in a collaborative manner. The enabling capabilities and building blocks are to be developed to a level such that the industrial entities may then be able to perform developments and eventually produce for concrete/more specific space related developments. The developments may go from a proof-of-concept (via simulation or experiment) up to an engineering qualification model (EQM). They address any technical area (structures, avionics/GNC, power control and distribution...). The spefications are to be linked to the guiding system or sub-system specifications. The maximum amount per activity is 1,000 K. The maximum duration is24 months.

original.description: The European Space Agency and the Ministry of Economy, Tourism and Sport of Slovenia hereby invite you to submit a proposal for theabove Call for Proposals, which will be soon published in esa-star. While it is made visible to all ESA Member States, Associate Members and European Cooperating States, this CfP will be addressed only to Slovenian legal entities registered in ESA-STAR, as prime tenderer and foresees the following standard activity types:Type A Research and Preparatory Activities, aimed at the preparation for participation in ESA optional programmes or the initial steps of a product development for Space, with potential for use on futureESA missions or commercial missions. The start TRL shall be at least 1 and the target TRL shall be TRL 3 or below. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 150,000.Type B Flight- and Ground Segment-related Research and Development Activities, targetting equipment to build competences and capabilities centred on products or generic technology development with potential for re-use on ESA or commercial missions. The start TRL shall be at least 3 and the target TRL shall be TRL 5. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 400 000 (flight related)/EUR 300 000 (ground related).Type C Flight Opportunities for mature existing Slovenian technologies or products in collaboration with experienced European players, to be involved in non-ESA mission in order to become flight proven. The start TRL shall be at least 5 and the target TRL shall be TRL 9. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 750 000 (inc. launch and operation cost). The work carried out by the Tenderer must be co-funded to a minimum level of 25% of the total cost of the activity. Maximum 20% of the budget may be assigned tonon-Slovenian entities, however launch and integration tasks are excluded from this limitation.Type D Space science activities, supporting the involvement of national researchers leading to potential of future involvement in ESA science mission core team and publication of peer reviewed scientific papers. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 100,000.Type F Space Applications, products and services making use of ESA/ European space infrastructure that is already existing or scheduled for operation in the near term. The start TRLshall be at least 6 and the target TRL shall be TRL 8. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 200,000. The work carried out by the Tenderer must be co-funded to a minimum level of 25% of the total cost of the activity.Type G1 University courses/modules leading to a qualification (BSc or MSc) in space related topics that correspond to the needs of national space industry and to encourage career in spaceandanswer to national space industry needs. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 70,000.To be published as a separate tender in esa-star: TypeG2 PhD Theses that correspond to a clear need from the national space industry and would lead to a new product or service beingableto be developed. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 70,000 with a minimum company co-funding of EUR 10,000. To be published in the Open Space Innovation Platform (OSIP, https://ideas.esa.int/): Type H  Space Related Training Courses, for the cost reimbursement of participation of employees in space related training courses. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 9,999. More information and further programmatic constraints can be consulted in the cover letter of the call upon its issue date.
